definitions.explanation: The closing part of a chapter in a book, especially the summaries or practice problems placed there in textbooks and study guides.

examples.japanese: {章末|しょうまつ}に{問題|もんだい}がある。
examples.english: There are problems at the end of the chapter.

examples.japanese: {章末|しょうまつ}のまとめを{読|よ}む。
examples.english: I read the summary at the end of the chapter.

examples.japanese: {各|かく}{章末|しょうまつ}に{練習|れんしゅう}{問題|もんだい}がついている{参考書|さんこうしょ}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose a study guide with practice problems at the end of each chapter.

notes:
Compound of {章|しょう} (chapter) + {末|まつ} (end). Refers to the tail end of a chapter, most often in the context of textbook material placed there.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {章末|しょうまつ}{問題|もんだい}: end-of-chapter problems
- {章末|しょうまつ}のまとめ: chapter-end summary

The opposite is {章|しょう}の{初|はじ}め (the beginning of a chapter).
